transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-16 14:30 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel (Redwood); Lena Müller, Carlos Ruiz, Priya Shah (EuroFin)

Summary (auto-gen): Quick security/compliance review focused on data residency and region pinning. EuroFin needs EU-only processing for payment PII, asks about cross-border fallback, sub-processors, and KMS/customer-managed keys. Redwood team explains hosted vs dedicated vs private options, region pinning mechanics, and encryption key options. Next steps: SOC2/ISO certs, region-pinning feasibility doc, follow-up architecture session.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Okay hi everyone, thanks for joining — can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Lena (EuroFin): Yes, loud and clear — thanks Maya.
[00:06] Samir (Redwood SE): Hi all, Samir here, I'll be covering technical bits, especially region routing and KMS options.
[00:12] Priya (EuroFin): Great thanks — we have a few people on the compliance side so I'll let Lena drive requirements.

[00:20] Lena: To set context, EuroFin handles EU cardholder data and certain PII that must remain in the EU. Our regulators require data residency for processing and storage. We saw your docs on region pinning but want to understand guarantee levels and fallback behaviors — e.g., if a pod in eu-west goes down does anything cross to the US or get queued? Also sub-processors, third-party metrics, and encryption key control.

[00:45] Maya: Totally. High level: Redwood supports region pinning for requests — requests can be routed to EU-only capacity. We have three deployment modes that are relevant: Hosted (multi-region but can pin), Dedicated (reserved EU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem) which gives most isolation. The guarantee depends on configuration — default hosted may route to nearest region, but we can enforce EU-only routing and prevent cross-border processing.

[01:10] Carlos: When you say enforce, is that a soft preference or hard guarantee? For compliance we need to be sure no tokens or KV cache data leaves EU.

[01:18] Samir: It's config-driven. For hard guarantees you want either Dedicated EU capacity or Private deployment. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools in the EU; we have SLA-backed throughput and the control plane can be configured to disallow fallback to non-EU regions. Hosted with pinning is possible but historically has a fallback policy for capacity shortages — we can remove fallback but that impacts availability.

[01:40] Lena: So what's the trade-off for removing fallback? Increased latency vs potential service degradation?

[01:44] Samir: Mainly availability and potentially higher cost. If there's no cross-region fallback and EU capacity is saturated you'd see request queuing or rejections. With fallback enabled, we route to a compatible variant in another region — which is the cross-border case you want to avoid.

[02:05] Priya: For Dedicated, can we have customer-managed KMS keys? Our security team insists on control of master keys.

[02:12] Maya: Yes, with Private we support full customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and HSM, and Dedicated supports customer KMS integrations in most cases. For hosted public API, BYOK is more limited — we use provider-managed keys but can enable envelope encryption with customer KMS for specific customers. I'll follow up with exact doc.

[02:34] Carlos: Any data that might go to logs or analytics streams — are those stored outside EU? We need audit logs to be EU-resident too.

[02:40] Samir: Good callout. Audit logs and traces are typically in the same region as processing when pinned; however some operational logs used for platform monitoring may be aggregated to other regions for reliability. For customers with strict residency we recommend Private with full control or Dedicated with log replay disabled and log retention in EU-only storage. We'll document the log flow in the feasibility.

[03:02] Lena: What about sub-processors — do you use any US-based sub-processors that would cause cross-border processing even if we pin to EU?

[03:09] Maya: We maintain a sub-processor list and SCCs where applicable. Some cloud infra providers or monitoring vendors may be US-based — for EU-only needs we can provide an allowed list and, in Dedicated/Private, reduce reliance on certain third parties. I will attach our current sub-processor list and the standard contractual clauses document.

[03:30] Carlos: Do you have documentation on Schrems II and how you implement SCCs?

[03:33] Samir: Yes — we have a compliance pack that includes SCCs, our data transfer assessments, and the approach to supplemental measures like encryption in transit and at rest. We'll share it.

[03:45] Priya: On the technical side — can you explain how region pinning is implemented? Is it DNS-level routing, or application layer routing with a control plane that pins requests to specific pools? Also how does that interact with KV cache or session state?

[04:00] Samir: It's application-layer routing in our control plane. Requests include a region tag at the front — either via API param, org-level policy, or per-route setting. The control plane routes to capacity pools in the target region and we maintain KV cache affinity for low-latency recurrent sessions. For pinned routes we prevent control-plane fallback. KV caches are per-region; we don't replicate KV cache cross-border for pinned workloads unless replication is explicitly enabled.

[04:30] Speaker 2 (Maya?): Sorry — did you say per-route or per-organization?
[04:33] Maya: Both — you can set org defaults and override per-route. For EuroFin you'd set an org-level EU-only policy and then pin critical routes.

[04:45] Lena: Is there any risk of metadata or anonymized telemetry still leaving EU?

[04:50] Samir: There is platform telemetry for health and capacity — for strict EU requirements we can opt into a reduced telemetry mode and route telemetry endpoints to EU collectors. That is more common in Dedicated/Private setups. We'll include flags in the doc.

[05:05] Priya: For encryption-at-rest, you mentioned envelope encryption — can you outline the key flow? Who has access to the master key?

[05:12] Samir: In typical hosted mode Redwood holds the master key managed by cloud provider KMS, and we use envelope keys per tenant. With BYOK or customer-managed KMS, the customer retains the master key and we only hold encrypted data keys. Access to master keys is controlled by KMS policies and we don't have plaintext access. For Private we can integrate with your HSM and KMS fully.

[05:35] Carlos: Does the platform support rotation of keys without downtime?

[05:38] Samir: Yes, key rotation is supported — we do background re-encryption for active data keys and issue new envelope keys. There may be transient performance impact but no planned downtime. We'll provide the rotation SLA.

[05:52] Lena: Can you confirm retention and deletion workflows? If we request deletion of EU PII, what's the guarantee that it's removed from backups and logs?

[05:58] Maya: Deletion pipeline: we mark data for deletion, remove active copies, and queue background jobs to purge backups per retention window. For Dedicated/Private we can negotiate shorter backup retention and provide attestations. Hosted has standard retention windows documented — we'll share the policy and a proposed shorter retention for your Dedicated pilot.

[06:20] Priya: Regarding audits, do you allow auditor access and logs for SOC 2? Do you support customer-led audits on Dedicated?

[06:27] Maya: Yes, SOC 2 reports are available. For Dedicated and Private, we support auditor access under NDA and can provide targeted logs for audit scope. Hosted customers get SOC 2 summary reports.

[06:38] Carlos: About cross-border fallback: if we disable fallback, what happens when EU capacity is at 100%? Can we set autoscale or burst into other EU regions only?

[06:47] Samir: You can configure autoscale within EU regions and a burst policy to other EU zones. We can also reserve burst capacity in a second EU region under Dedicated. The primary risk is cost — reserved burst capacity increases commitment. We'll map out options with cost estimates.

[07:05] Lena: One last technical question: for the control plane itself, where is it hosted? Any control-plane metadata that could be sent to US?

[07:12] Samir: Control plane is multi-region; some control plane services are global. For high-compliance customers we offer a private control plane option that can be run in EU and minimize metadata transfer. We'll include the private control plane architecture in the follow-up.

[07:30] Speaker 3 (Lena): Okay that helps — I just want to be clear on the options: 1) Hosted with EU pinning but possibly fallback (less guarantee); 2) Dedicated EU pools (stronger guarantee + SLA); 3) Private/VPC (full control incl KMS and control plane). Is that fair?

[07:45] Maya: Exactly. And we can mix options — start hosted with pinning for evaluation and move to Dedicated or Private for production.

[07:55] Priya: For PCI implications, do you have any PCI-specific guidance? Our PCI team will likely require extra segmentation.

[08:02] Samir: We have PCI guidance in our compliance pack; typically Dedicated or Private is recommended for the highest PCI scopes. We'll call out segmentation patterns and recommended network controls.

[08:15] Carlos: Any mention of sub-processors again — specifically telemetry vendors or SSO providers?

[08:20] Maya: We'll share the sub-processor list. For SSO we integrate with customer IdP via SAML/SCIM; SSO metadata doesn't contain PII typically. If you need an EU-only IdP integration path we can work with you.

[08:32] Lena: Ok, let's capture next steps and owners.

[08:35] Maya: Sure — I'll read them back: 1) Maya to send SOC2, ISO27001 scope, sub-processor list, SCCs (by Friday 12/18). 2) Samir to deliver region pinning feasibility doc, network diagram, and telemetry flow that shows logs/backup boundaries (by 12/22). 3) EuroFin (Priya) to share exact EU regions required and retention policy (by 12/20). 4) Schedule follow-up architecture deep dive and pilot kickoff week of 12/29. Anything to add?

[09:05] Lena: That looks right. Also please include cost estimate options for Dedicated burst/reserved capacity.

[09:12] Maya: Got it — cost estimates will be included in the feasibility doc.

[09:18] Priya: Quick clarifying Q — for the KV cache, is the cache encrypted at rest and isolated per-tenant?

[09:24] Samir: Yes, KV caches are tenant-scoped and encrypted at rest. In EU-pinned setups we keep cache shards in-region. We'll add a diagram.

[09:36] Carlos: Any immediate blockers from our side? I don't think so — we need the docs and then legal will review SCCs and procurement.

[09:42] Maya: Great. We'll follow up with the packet. Thanks all for time.

[09:46] Lena: Thanks Maya and Samir.
[09:48] Priya: Thanks.

Recap / Close:
- Action items tracked above.
- Follow-up: Architecture deep dive and pilot kickoff tentatively week of 2026-12-29.
- Attachments to be sent: SOC2 report, ISO27001 scope, sub-processor list, SCCs, region-pinning feasibility doc + cost estimates, telemetry/log flow diagram.

End of transcript.
